Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake — Acme Health (recap + next steps)

Hi Alice —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps for the POC/trial:

- Objective: Validate generation latency, cost per 1M tokens, and model quality for clinical note generation (structured template -> filled notes).
- Success criteria (initial): p50 latency < 200ms for typical prompts, p95 < 600ms; acceptable hallucination rate < 2% on our test set; accuracy on entity extraction >= 95%.
- Evaluation plan: provide a 10k-prompt test set (you mentioned a ~10k sample), Redwood will run end-to-end perf + quality evals using the same prompts and your rubric, share results and a breakdown by prompt length.
- Timeline: 2-week technical trial (env + workload ingestion + evals), followed by a 1-week extension if we need more data. Target kickoff: next Tuesday (2027-03-08).
- Ownership & roles: Ben (sales) = program lead; Dylan (engineer) = technical POC; Marissa (sales ops) = contracting/finance.

To help Dylan size the trial infra, please fill out the attached workload-intake-template.xlsx with approximate values for: steady RPS, peak burst RPS, avg/95th token lengths, concurrent requests, expected evaluation dataset size, and any long-tail patterns. If easier, paste numbers in a reply.

Attachments: workload-intake-template.xlsx (simple XLSX with fields we need).

Proposed next steps:
1) Alice fills intake or replies with numbers by EOD Friday (2027-03-04)
2) Dylan schedules 30-min technical onboarding to provision trial environment
3) We provision reserved trial capacity and run the first eval within 48 hours of intake receipt.

Let me know if that matches your expectations. Thanks again — excited to get this running.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — Acme Health (recap + next steps)

Ben — thanks for the recap. This aligns well. I pasted the intake numbers below and attached a small sample CSV of prompts.

Intake (approx):
- Steady-state RPS: 2 requests/sec
- Peak burst RPS: 20 requests/sec (short bursts, ~30–60s)
- Typical prompt token length (input): 40
- Typical response token length (output): 50–80
- 95th percentile token length (combined): ~220 tokens
- Concurrent outstanding requests: 5–10 (mostly from background jobs + web UI)
- Test dataset: 10,000 prompts (mix of short/long templates).
- Special patterns: several templates require multi-turn context reuse (KV-cache reuse across requests for same patient session).

Attachments: acme_sample_prompts.csv

Success criteria: agree with your suggested metrics; additionally, we want to measure cost per 1M tokens and whether throughput scales linearly across dedicated nodes.

We can get the filled XLSX by Friday if helpful, but the numbers above should be sufficient to size the trial.

Thanks,
Alice

Quick clarification/questions before the call:
1) Authentication: do you want us to integrate via API key over the public endpoint or a private VPC peering for the trial? (VPC will take longer to provision).
2) For KV-cache reuse: are sessions keyed by patient_id or a different session_id? This affects routing and affinity config.
3) Do you have a small set of long-tail worst-case prompts we should seed the 95th/99th percentile tests with? If yes, please attach or point to a Drive link.

I’ve attached a starter config we’ll use for the trial (poc_trial_config.json) — contains default batching, max tokens, and latency SLOs — we’ll tweak after intake.
